Considering it is a free app to support a $20 fitness band, it's a great value. It does have a few quirks, but it is functional. The most serious deficit it's the lack of US customary measurements. The app is solely metric with no option to display temperature in°F or distance in miles. English captions are a bit oddly phrased, but still intelligible (e.g. "Beyond 65% get up early compare to Male users in the same age group."). Sleep tracking is incomplete until after 10:00AM. Every morning it looks like I got up at midnight after only 2 hours of sleep, but updates sometime after 10:00AM to show the remainder of the previous night's sleep. It does distinguish between awake, light sleep and heavy sleep. Others complain that step tracking is inaccurate, but it's accurate for me. The sensor is measuring the shock of each step through the band on your wrist, not on your feet. If your stride is so soft that it doesn't bounce your wrist, the steps won't be counted. There's an option to measure and record heart rate automatically throughout the day, but BP and O2 saturation are only measured and logged when requested. I'd like to see trend of O2 saturation recorded overnight while I'm sleeping (to confirm or rule out apnea events as the reason for any disruptions in my sleep patterns).
